Lately, I’ve been receiving a lot of DMs about the Allianz Tech Championship interview process, so I thought I’d share some tips to help you ace it: 

1. Approach with Confidence and Collaboration
The interview is more of a dialogue than a test. The panel is keen on your ideas and how they can translate into impactful solutions. Stay calm and focused—it’s a two-way street. 

2. Understand Your Work
You should be comfortable talking about your project—the 'why' behind your choices and its potential impact are always good starting points.

3. Embrace the Learning Opportunity
Treat the interview as more than just an evaluation. The panel consists of experts who can provide invaluable insights. You’ll leave the room smarter than when you entered!💡I deleted around 6000 unnecessary pictures from my cloud storage after Rahul Sir introduced me to the harm it causes to the environment. 

4. Authenticity is Key
Be honest and transparent with your responses. Authenticity resonates with interviewers and leaves a lasting impression. 

Bonus Tip: If you blank out during a question, just remember—Ctrl+Z doesn’t work in real life, but a quick pause and a thoughtful answer can save the day! 

Through this initiative, Allianz is doing an amazing job of nurturing young tech talent and helping us grow. I’m genuinely grateful for such platforms.

Good luck to everyone preparing—keep learning and enjoying the process! If you have more questions, feel free to drop a message or comment below. Let’s learn and grow together.

🌀 Ideas in Motion — We Spun Things Around!

Today marked the kickoff of our flagship event planning, and this time, we did things a little differently — with a twist (literally)!

After attending countless traditional meetings in my junior year, I knew how quickly the energy in a room can fade. So instead of sticking to the usual format, we added a playful twist: Spin the Bottle style brainstorming!

Here’s how it worked:

➡️ If the bottle pointed at you, you shared an idea — be it about themes, poster designs, or engagement strategies.
➡️ If the bottle pointed away from you, you got to assign a fun challenge or target to another team member.

The outcome?
We laughed, we shared wildly creative ideas, we cheered each other on — and most importantly, we felt connected. It didn’t feel like work; it felt like building something meaningful together.

Moments like these remind me why I love what I do — and more importantly, why I love this team - ACM-W CCEW Chapter Cummins, Pune 💙
Everyone brought their energy, their voice, and their heart into that circle. And I know this is just the beginning of something incredible. Really grateful to Dr. Sandhya Arora ma'am for her support.

If you're someone who believes that leadership doesn’t have to be rigid — that collaboration can be joyful and planning can be personal — I’d love to connect and hear how your team brings ideas to life.

Stop Scrolling! You Need to Know Why IPv6 is the Next Big Thing!

We’ve all heard it: “We’re running out of IP addresses!” Enter IPv6, the hero with more addresses than we’ll ever need (seriously, trillions upon trillions). But this isn’t just a story about more numbers. It’s a tale of how the Internet itself is evolving in ways that go far beyond those little dot-separated digits. 
 IPv6 isn’t just about fixing the awkward “out of room” moment caused by IPv4’s 4.3 billion addresses. It’s about what happens when scarcity vanishes entirely. Imagine suddenly having infinite storage on your phone—what would you focus on? Probably everything except storage. 

That’s exactly what the Internet is doing. Instead of fretting over how to squeeze everyone onto the network, it’s now all about what we do once we’re there. Applications, services, and experiences have taken center stage, and the network is happy to sit back and play its role as the reliable foundation. 
Let’s be honest: IPv4 is like that old phone you keep around because it still works (kinda). NAT ( 
hashtag
#Network Address Translation) and clever hacks have kept it alive, even as IPv6 sits there, shiny and ready to take over. But here’s the thing: IPv4’s continued use isn’t about preference; it’s about momentum. Shifting global infrastructure is like trying to steer a cruise ship with a canoe paddle—it’s slow, messy, and nobody’s having fun. 

The switch to IPv6 is about more than tech. It’s about the Internet economy evolving. Back in the 
hashtag
#IPv4 days, the network itself was the hot commodity. Scarcity of addresses meant communication capability was the prize. Now? With 
hashtag
#IPv6, that scarcity is gone, and the economic action has shifted up the stack. 
 The real game is happening where apps and services live. Whether it’s your favorite streaming platform, AI chatbots, or immersive VR worlds, it’s the what that matters now—not the how. Companies are no longer competing over bandwidth and addresses; they’re racing to deliver the smartest, fastest, and coolest applications. Without the limits of address scarcity, developers are free to think bigger, connecting more devices, deploying smarter networks, and enabling services we haven’t even dreamed of yet. 

Now you might be wondering, What Does This Mean for Us?
As IPv6 adoption grows, we’re moving into an Internet that’s less about “Can we connect?” and more about “What incredible things can we do once we’re connected?” 
The real story isn’t about IPv6 replacing IPv4—it’s about how this shift is redefining what the Internet is for. So buckle up, because the best days of the Internet aren’t behind us; they’re just getting started.

The interview is more of a dialogue than a test. The panel is keen on your ideas and how they can translate into impactful solutions. Stay calm and focused—it’s a two-way street.

You should be comfortable talking about your project—the 'why' behind your choices and its potential impact are always good starting points.

Treat the interview as more than just an evaluation. The panel consists of experts who can provide invaluable insights. You’ll leave the room smarter than when you entered!💡I deleted around 6000 unnecessary pictures from my cloud storage after Rahul Sir introduced me to the harm it causes to the environment.

Bonus Tip: If you blank out during a question, just remember—Ctrl+Z doesn’t work in real life, but a quick pause and a thoughtful answer can save the day!

When do you foresee the need to move beyond Internet Protocols (IP)?

This was something that I asked today as I had the privilege of attending an enlightening co-teaching session led by the renowned Dr. R (Venki) Venkateswaran Sir , an ACM Distinguished Speaker. The session, part of the Teacher Partnership Program by ACM India , offered deep insights into the Data Link Layer and critical features of IP protocols.

One of the most engaging moments was a practical demonstration that illustrated essential concepts of IP protocols and packet-switching networks. Two messages were passed from two separate sources to different destinations in the auditorium. These messages were fragmented into 5 parts and transmitted via different paths (students). The outcome was revealing: one recipient received all 5 packets but in a random order, demonstrating IP’s lack of in-order delivery guarantee, while the other received only 1 packet, highlighting packet loss. This activity effectively demonstrated how IP operates in a best-effort delivery model and lacks reliability and sequencing, key services provided by higher layers like TCP.

When Dr. Venkateswaran remarked that IP is "just good enough" for most modern applications, I couldn’t resist asking, "When do you foresee the need to move beyond IP?" His insightful response—"It will take long enough"—made me reflect on the resilience and adaptability of IP in today’s networks and how far-reaching its influence is, even as we anticipate future advances in networking protocols.

I'm deeply grateful to MKSSS Cummins College of Engineering for Women , Dr. Supriya Kelkar ma'am, meenal Kamlakar ma'am and Dr.Mahendra Deore Sir for facilitating such an insightful session, and I look forward to more such thought-provoking discussions. Special thanks to ACM India for fostering such opportunities that blend academic and practical learning!
